## Assessing predicted probabilities

$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_i  &\sim Bernoulli(p_i) \\
\log \left( \dfrac{\widehat{\pi}_i}{1 - \widehat{\pi}_i} \right) &= \beta_0 + \beta_1 X_{i1} + \cdots + \beta_k X_{ik}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Question:** How do we tell if $\widehat{\pi}_i$ is a "good" estimator of $\pi_i$?

\vspace{5cm}

## Assessing predicted probabilities

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmhelpR)
library(patchwork)

m_dengue <- glm(Dengue ~ WBC, data = dengue, family = binomial)
m_dengue2 <- glm(Dengue ~ log(WBC), data = dengue, family = binomial)

p1 <- dengue |>
  mutate(residuals = statmod::qresid(m_dengue)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = WBC, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(size=0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Randomized quantile residuals",
       title = "Logistic regression of \n Dengue on WBC")

p2 <- dengue |>
  mutate(residuals = statmod::qresid(m_dengue2)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log(WBC), y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(size=0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Randomized quantile residuals",
       title = "Logistic regression of \n Dengue on log(WBC)")
p1 + p2
```

\vspace{1.5cm}

**Question:** Does using WBC vs. log(WBC) make a difference for the quality of our predictions?



## Calibration plot

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
p3 <- calibration_plot(m_dengue$fitted.values, m_dengue$y,
                       num_bins = 12) +
  labs(title = "Logistic regression with WBC") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 10))
p4 <- calibration_plot(m_dengue2$fitted.values,
                       m_dengue2$y) +
  labs(title = "Logistic regression with log(WBC)") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 10))

(p1 + p2)/(p3 + p4)
```

## Parametric bootstrap + visual inference

```{r, include=F}
cal_data <- function(pred, y, group, num_bins = 10,
                     use_data_range = F){
  dat <- data.frame(pred, y)
  
  if(!missing(group)){
    if(length(pred) != length(group)){
      stop("Predictions (pred) and group labels (group) must have the same length")
    }
    
    dat <- dat |>
      dplyr::mutate(group = as.factor(group))
  } else {
    dat <- dat |>
      dplyr::mutate(group = "")
  }
  
  if(use_data_range){
    xmin <- min(pred)
    xmax <- max(pred)
  } else {
    xmin <- 0
    xmax <- 1
  }
  break_pts <- seq(xmin, xmax, length = num_bins + 1)
  
  dat <- dat |>
    tidyr::drop_na()
  
  dat |>
    dplyr::mutate(bin = cut(pred, breaks = break_pts)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(group, bin) |>
    dplyr::summarize(pred = mean(pred), prop = mean(y), n = dplyr::n(),
                     sm = sum(y),
                     lower = stats::binom.test(sm, n)$conf.int[1],
                     upper = stats::binom.test(sm, n)$conf.int[2],
                     .groups = "drop")
}
```

```{r, echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
library(regressinator)
library(tidyverse)
bootstrap_cal <- function(f){
  pred <- f$fitted.values
  y <- f$y
  cal_data(pred, y, num_bins = 12)
}

model_lineup(m_dengue, fn = bootstrap_cal, nsim = 20) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(x = pred,
                                      ymin=lower,
                                      ymax=upper),
                         width=.05,
                         color = "orange") +
  geom_point(aes(x = pred, y = prop), size=0.75) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, lty = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Predicted probability", y = "Observed proportion") +
  facet_wrap(vars(.sample)) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.x = element_blank())
```

## Class activity

```{r, include=F}
titanic <- read.csv("https://sta214-f26.github.io/homework/Titanic.csv")

titanic_small <- titanic |>
  drop_na(Age)

m_titanic <- glm(Survived ~ Age, 
                 data = titanic_small, family = binomial)
```

```{r, echo=F, message=F, fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
calibration_plot(m_titanic$fitted.values,
                       m_titanic$y,
                       group = titanic_small$Sex,
                       use_data_range = T) +
  labs(title = "Age only, plotted by Sex")
```

## Class activity

```{r echo=F, message=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=3}
m_titanic2 <- glm(Survived ~ Age + Sex + as.factor(Pclass), 
                 data = titanic_small, family = binomial)

calibration_plot(m_titanic2$fitted.values,
                       m_titanic2$y,
                       use_data_range = T,
                 num_bins = 12) +
  labs(title = "Age, Sex, Pclass")
```

## Visual inference

```{r, echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
set.seed(5)
model_lineup(m_titanic2, fn = bootstrap_cal, nsim = 20) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(x = pred,
                             ymin=lower,
                             ymax=upper),
                width=.05,
                color = "orange") +
  geom_point(aes(x = pred, y = prop), size=0.75) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, lty = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Predicted probability", y = "Observed proportion") +
  facet_wrap(vars(.sample)) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text.x = element_blank())
```
